outcome: Pelvic Organ Prolapse Distress Inventory (POPDI) scores
cohort: The study included women who had their first vaginal birth, comparing cases with III- and IV-degree vaginal tears (OASI) to controls with intact perineum or I- and II-degree vaginal tears.
finding: Major vaginal tears (III- and IV-degree lacerations/OASI) demonstrated a strong correlation with the persistence of pelvic floor dysfunction, particularly intestinal symptoms, and a significant negative impact on women's quality of life up to 12 months after delivery.
